facts.raw_span: a woman in her 60s presented with an itchy plaque on the mid-back
had had a lesion at that site since childhood, which had remained asymptomatic and pea sized for most of that time
over the 10 years prior to presentation it had gradually increased in size and became itchy
occasional oozing of serosanguineous fluid and bleeding from the lesion
1.5 × 1.0-cm well-defined erythematous plaque with overlying ulceration on the mid-back, 1 cm left of the spine
adjoining skin showed a horseshoe-shaped oval area of lichenification
Histopathological examination: Revealed a circumscribed tumor contiguous with adjoining normal epidermis and delineated from underlying dermis by continuous apocrine epithelial lining
tumor epithelium with multiple papillary projections with vascular, plasma cell–rich stroma
several foci showed papillary projections lined by multilayered epithelium with atypical cells, few mitotic figures, and areas of necrosis but no dermal invasion
p63 staining positive in myoepithelial cell layers
adjacent skin showed dermal papillae with congophilic amorphous eosinophilic deposits
pan-cytokeratin (AE1/3) immunostain positive

concepts.why: The presence of a circumscribed tumor with papillary projections and a vascular, plasma cell-rich stroma is consistent with hidradenoma papilliferum.
The tumor's apocrine epithelial lining and positive p63 staining in myoepithelial cell layers support the diagnosis of syringocystadenoma papilliferum.
The presence of a tumor with multiple papillary projections and a positive pan-cytokeratin immunostain is consistent with eccrine poroma.
The well-defined erythematous plaque with overlying ulceration and adjoining skin showing lichenification is consistent with seborrheic keratosis.
The presence of a well-defined erythematous plaque with overlying ulceration and adjoining skin showing lichenification is also consistent with dermatofibroma.
The rapid growth and presence of atypical cells, mitotic figures, and areas of necrosis are consistent with keratoacanthoma.
The presence of atypical cells, mitotic figures, and areas of necrosis, as well as a positive pan-cytokeratin immunostain, are consistent with squamous cell carcinoma.
The presence of a well-defined erythematous plaque with overlying ulceration and atypical cells, mitotic figures, and areas of necrosis are consistent with basal cell carcinoma.

rationales.F12: Pan-cytokeratin immunostain positive is consistent with the epithelial origin of the tumor.
